```

The issue is: when we access `d[a[i]]`, we need to prove `0 <= a[i] < d.Length`. We know `d.Length = a.Length - 2`. The precondition gives us `-1 <= a[i] < a.Length - 2`, so `a[i] < d.Length` and `a[i] >= -1`. But we need `a[i] >= 0` for the index to be valid.

```
requires forall i :: 0 <= i < a.Length ==> -1 <= a[i] < a.Length - 2;

This is a `requires` issue. The proof obligation is `initiation` because at the start of the loop (i=0), when we try to access `d[a[i]]`, we can't prove the index is in range because the precondition allows `a[i] = -1`.

The proof obligation is about initiation because at the start of the loop (before any iteration), we need to be able to access `d[a[i]]` with `i = 0`, and the precondition doesn't guarantee `a[0] >= 0`.

Actually, it could also be preservation - after updating `i`, we need to be able to access `d[a[i]]` for the new value of `i`. But the same issue applies - the precondition is the source of the problem.

The spec element is `requires` and the proof obligation is `initiation` (the precondition doesn't establish that `a[i] >= 0` for the index access into `d`).
